name: Respects the explicit null guard vs. lists NullPointerException as a live risk at that line
side_a: No deduction when the answer confines the exception to the cast (ClassCastException) and does not claim a NullPointerException can occur on that line — i.e. it accounts for (or at least does not contradict) the explicit null check that already guards the fragment reference.
side_b: Deduct when the answer asserts a NullPointerException as a possible exception at that line, since the code's `if (... != null)` guard rules it out; naming NPE shows the answer is listing generic exception types rather than reading the actual control flow.

name: States the causal mechanism of the exception vs. enumerates exception type names
side_a: No deduction when the answer ties the exception to a concrete mechanism in the code — which value is cast, to what, and under what condition it fails.
side_b: Deduct when the answer only enumerates exception class names (optionally with boilerplate advice) without explaining what in the code would produce them.

name: Acknowledges the null/NPE branch vs. mentions only the cast-type failure
side_a: no_deduct — the answer explicitly raises the null case: either names NullPointerException as a possible exception at the line, or reasons about the null-returning/null-check behavior of findFragmentById.
side_b: deduct — the answer conditions the exception solely on the fragment being the wrong type (interface not implemented) and never mentions null, a missing fragment, or NullPointerException, pushing all other possibilities into vague 'other runtime exceptions'.

name: Vague/hedged mention of 'other possible' exceptions vs concretely naming a specific extra exception (SecurityException) with a cause
side_a: Give credit if, beyond the fragment-cast exception, the answer only gestures vaguely at unspecified further possibilities (e.g., 'other runtime exceptions could occur depending on the implementation / system constraints') without naming a concrete exception type tied to a different API call — the hedge adds no false claim about this line.
side_b: Deduct 2 points if the answer concretely names an additional exception type and attributes it to a specific other operation or simply lists it as an outcome of this line (e.g., 'SecurityException if foreground service start fails due to permission issues', or a flat list 'RuntimeException, or SecurityException'), since this asserts a specific wrong exception for the asked line.

name: correct type singled out as the primary/attributed cause vs flat undifferentiated shotgun list of types
side_a: No deduction when the answer identifies ClassCastException as the primary/most-likely exception at the lookup-and-cast site (ranked with words like 'most likely', 'particularly', 'will be thrown if...', or leading a short list of types that are each plausible at that same lookup), with any extra types subordinated or tied to a stated cause/other operation. The extra names then read as secondary caveats rather than competing claims about the asked line.
side_b: Deduct when the answer just sprays an undifferentiated list of exception classes over 'this code' with no ranking, no mechanism, and no attribution — so each named type (NullPointerException, RuntimeException, SecurityException) stands as an equal claim about what the asked line throws, including catch-all/irrelevant types.

name: States the triggering condition for the exception vs merely enumerates exception class names
side_a: No deduct as long as the answer states the condition that produces the failure — i.e., an 'if/when the fragment returned is not of that type / does not implement that interface' style clause attached to the cast. The answer may additionally list other speculative exceptions without losing the point, provided one candidate is tied to a stated triggering condition.
side_b: Deduct when the answer only enumerates exception class names (e.g. 'ClassCastException or NullPointerException', 'NullPointerException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException, or SecurityException') with no stated condition under which any of them would arise; an undifferentiated laundry list of possible exception types does not count as identifying the failure.

name: Names NullPointerException (alongside ClassCastException) as a possible exception vs confines the answer to ClassCastException only
side_a: Credit if the answer explicitly names NullPointerException (or an equivalent null-dereference failure) among the exceptions that can occur at this line, in addition to the cast failure.
side_b: Deduct if the answer identifies only ClassCastException as the concrete exception, leaving null-dereference either unmentioned or dismissed/relegated to vague 'other runtime exceptions'.

name: Commits to one correct exception (ClassCastException) vs shotgun-lists several speculative exception types
side_a: No deduct if the answer names ClassCastException as the exception and confines itself to that mechanism, without appending a list of other possible exception types.
side_b: Deduct if the answer, in addition to ClassCastException, enumerates other speculative exception types (NullPointerException, SecurityException, RuntimeException, etc.) as things that 'could also' happen.

name: Treats the null check as excluding NPE vs claims NullPointerException is still possible
side_a: No deduct if the answer accounts for the existing null check and does not claim a NullPointerException can occur at this line.
side_b: Deduct if the answer asserts NullPointerException as a possible exception at this line even though the code null-checks the fragment before use.

name: Addresses the null/NullPointerException possibility of findFragmentById vs. only the wrong-type cast
side_a: No deduction if the answer engages with the null-return/NullPointerException branch of `findFragmentById` — either by naming NullPointerException as a possible exception or by explicitly reasoning about the null check — in addition to the ClassCastException.
side_b: Deduct if the answer treats the wrong-type cast as the only concretely identified failure and never mentions a null fragment / NullPointerException, filling the remainder with an unnamed catch-all ("other runtime exceptions could occur") pinned to downstream calls.
